questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(8,-3,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-⟨7,-2,4⟩)\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=0.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(7,-2,4).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨7,-2,4⟩-⟨8,-3,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2-3-6|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,3,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩ & =16 \\ -2x-3y+6z & =16 \\ 2x & =6z-3y-16 \\ x & =3z-\frac{3}{2}y-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $y=2$ and $z=1,$ we get 

$$
x=3-\frac{3}{2}(2)-8=-8.
$$

So, the point $Q(-8,2,1)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-8,2,1⟩-⟨5,3,7⟩ \\  & =⟨-13,-1,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-13)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-6)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|26+3-36|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,3,-6)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-x+2y+2z=8.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-2$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+2y+2z & =8 \\ -1(-2)+2(1)+2z & =8 \\ 2z & =4 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-2,1,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-2,1,2⟩-⟨-2,3,-6⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-1,2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|0\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+8\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|0-4+16|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|12|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{12}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+6|}{\sqrt{4+0+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,8\,|}{\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Cartesian Form
canonical_examples.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(3 , -10 , 3)$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equation $2x+y-2z = -1$.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=4$ and $y=-5$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z & =-1 \\ 2(4)+(-5)+1 & =2z \\ 4 & =2z \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(4, -5, 2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overrightarrow{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-5,2⟩-⟨3,-10,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $\mathbf{n}=\langle a,b,c \rangle.$ So, for the plane $\Pi,$ we have $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 1, -2 \rangle.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+5\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+5+2|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,9\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$
